voice: A period Irish-American New York policeman with natural cadence and idiom, standard spelling, and no stage-Irish caricature.

entries.text: Hey, now! Keep your hands off those notices.
A cut in the department's budget and another year of stuffed cabbage and cabbage soup. Now aren't you sorry you asked?
As far as I know, he's a good, law-abiding citizen.
I wouldn't care to be hit by one.
I'm not assigned to that case, miss. Why not ask Detective O'Riley? He's the man you should be talking to.
It's a popular dance, miss. It's also the you-know-what for the you-know-what I mentioned earlier.
She's a wealthy lady and one of our finest upstanding citizens. Never had cause to meet her personally, you understand.
Only that I'd be using one myself if I weren't on duty.
Go on with you. You're pulling my leg. There's no such man, is there now?
I haven't been working on the case, miss. You'll have to ask Detective O'Riley.
That's an obvious question, isn't it? A clever crook can get past a lock without a key.
Miss, I don't even know what you're asking about.
Not much, miss, but I'll gladly answer any questions you have about uniforms.
Not a thing, miss. It's only a flower shop, isn't it?
Not me, miss, but I could ask my good wife for you.
Well, it usually doesn't taste as good as the fattening stuff.
Ah, then I'm afraid I can't help you, miss. I've never heard of the fellow.
A very fine establishment, and worth seeing even if you're only in town a short while. Very educational.
But I live in this city. I don't have to visit every landmark.
The best advice I can offer, miss, is to keep some money in your shoe. You never know when you might need emergency cash.
They're very handy for taking notes, miss.
I should hope so, miss. He's the detective on duty today. His office is right over there if you want to speak with him.
And here I thought he was in such a good mood today. He's a busy man. If you spoke with him once, I doubt he'll see you again.
I've never heard of the fellow.
The Fourteenth Precinct, miss, and a fine precinct it is.
Ah, the bane of my existence: letting nosy reporters in where they're not wanted.
They're best with corned beef, if you'll pardon my opinion, with rye and mustard. White or wheat bread will do, or a kaiser roll. Bagels, too, if you don't mind chewing cement.
Now, I know nothing about any speakeasy in this town. We run a clean city here. But there are places where a lady can sit, relax, and enjoy a bit of the high life, if you follow me.
Some of those places are restricted, of course. You'll need to give them the right sign so they know you're all right.
Just mention the Charleston and the door will open for you. Have you got that?
Don't mention it--and I mean that. Don't go mentioning it to anyone.
I try not to trouble myself over little things like that, miss.
Yes, ma'am, and a fine, upstanding building it is.
Ah, well, I wouldn't know anything about that.
Now, you keep away from Yvette. I haven't seen her in ages and don't plan to see her again, so let sleeping dogs lie.
What would a young woman like you want with scum like that?
I suppose it's no secret, not around here. Ziggy is a first-class rat. He couldn't make it as a crook himself, so now he spoils things for the rest of them.
A nasty little bigmouth, though he does hear an awful lot. If you're looking for him, he's the sort who hangs around speakeasies.
No, thank you, miss. I prefer arm wrestling.
Here now, don't be touching the goods, miss.
I think I'll stick with my regulation uniform, if it's all the same to you.
Here now! Stop that!
I won't be needing one of those, miss. I already have one from supply.
That will come in handy for you, miss, so you hold on to it.
Is that a corned-beef sandwich on rye? Bless you, miss, I don't mind if I do.
And it tastes fresh, too. Marvellous.
There's no denying that, miss. Now, what was it you wanted to ask me?
Then take yourself down to the library.
Oh, well, strike up the band. Look, miss, I've been on my feet all day, I haven't had my lunch, and I've better things to do than chat with some slip of a girl reporter. Run along now.
